title: Computer Science Methodologies
purpose: Seed computer-science inquiry methods so Lantern can reason about algorithms, specifications, proofs, testing, benchmarking, profiling, simulation, reproducibility and adversarial evaluation while distinguishing evidence of behavior from guarantees of correctness.

concepts.definition: A finite/effective procedure for transforming inputs/state toward outputs under a specified computational model.
A declared description of required/allowed behavior, interfaces, invariants and constraints against which an implementation can be evaluated.
A concrete realization of an algorithm/system under a language/runtime/hardware environment.
Mathematical demonstration that a model/implementation satisfies a formal specification under stated assumptions.
A proof that an algorithm/program property follows from a formal specification/model; guarantee is bounded by specification/model/assumptions.
Test of a bounded component/behavior.
Test of interactions among components/interfaces.
End-to-end test of a system against specified behavior.
Generation of many inputs to test general invariants/properties rather than only hand-selected examples.
Automated generation/mutation of unusual inputs to discover crashes, invalid states or security failures.
Test preserving previously demonstrated behavior across changes.
Standardized workload/metric used to compare performance/capability under defined conditions.
Measurement of runtime resource behavior such as time, memory, CPU, I/O or energy to locate costs/bottlenecks.
Analysis of resource growth as input/problem size changes under a computational model.
Growth-rate characterization such as O(n), abstracting constants/lower-order terms; not a direct runtime measurement.
Observed performance on particular hardware/software/workloads.
Removal/disablement of a component to estimate its contribution to measured behavior.
Execution of a computational model to study its consequences; validity depends on model/implementation/input assumptions.
Ability to reproduce computational results from preserved code, data, environment/configuration and procedure.
Deliberate search for inputs/conditions that violate intended behavior or assumptions.
Implementation used as a comparison oracle/baseline, which itself may contain limitations/errors.
Difficulty determining the correct output for arbitrary test cases, especially complex systems.

guards.reason: Tests cover sampled/constructed cases unless exhaustive proof conditions apply.
Verification proves conformance to a formal specification, not that the specification captured the intended real-world requirement.
Unobserved failures may remain outside tested conditions.
Benchmarks measure selected workloads/metrics and can omit important capability/resource/safety dimensions.
Constants, input size, hardware and implementation can dominate practical runtime.
Reference implementations are useful oracles/baselines but may contain defects or scope limits.
Components interact; ablation estimates contribution under a specific system/configuration.
A reproducible computation can consistently implement a flawed method/model.
Simulation output is conditional on computational/model assumptions.
Resource efficiency and capability are separate evaluation dimensions.
Code size does not establish quality/capability and can increase complexity/risk.

invariants: Correctness is relative to a specification/model and assumptions.
Tests provide behavioral evidence; non-exhaustive tests are not universal proofs.
A failing test can reveal implementation defects, specification mismatch or test/oracle problems and should be diagnosed.
Formal verification does not guarantee that the formal specification captures the real intended requirement.
Benchmarks are scoped measurements, not universal rankings.
Asymptotic complexity and empirical runtime are distinct.
Profiling measures actual resource cost under declared workloads/environments.
Regression tests protect previously demonstrated capabilities.
Ablation provides evidence about component contribution while preserving interaction uncertainty.
Adversarial/fuzz/property-based testing complements ordinary examples by searching failure space.
Capability, resource efficiency, safety, maintainability and correctness remain separate evaluation dimensions.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core theoretical/empirical computer-science methodology, software testing, formal methods, benchmarking, profiling and reproducibility adapted to Lantern's self-evaluation architecture.
